skill.name: crack-hashcat
skill.description: Guides authorized password hash auditing with Hashcat, including hash identification, attack selection, session management, result analysis, and defensive reporting.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized Hashcat password audit workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in the auxiliary templates are false positives from documentation examples, placeholder rules, or CI sample code. The core SKILL.md content is confirmed high risk because it teaches credential hash extraction and Hashcat cracking workflows, including protected system password files. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill includes commands that extract hashes from /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, and Active Directory database material.
remediation.suggestion: Remove direct extraction commands or replace them with non-operational guidance that requires documented authorization and synthetic lab data.

remediation.issue: The skill gives operational cracking workflows for several credential sources.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit preflight gate requiring scope, owner approval, retention limits, and safe handling before any command examples are shown.

remediation.issue: The CI template uses a remote install script piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell installer with a pinned release artifact, checksum verification, or package manager installation.

remediation.issue: Generic template files create many static security hits unrelated to this Hashcat skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unused templates from the package or clearly separate them from runtime skill guidance.

content.value_statement: Security teams need controlled ways to test password resilience. This skill guides authorized Hashcat audits, hash identification, attack selection, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common Hashcat modes for MD5, SHA, NTLM, bcrypt, WPA, and Kerberos hashes.
Plans dictionary, brute-force, mask, hybrid, and rule-based cracking workflows.
Explains Hashcat session handling, restore behavior, status checks, and benchmark use.
Shows how to summarize cracked password results for policy and control improvements.
Includes authorization, chain-of-custody, storage, and cleanup guidance for sensitive artifacts.
limitations: It requires clear authorization and does not validate legal scope for the user.
It depends on Hashcat, compatible drivers, wordlists, and suitable compute hardware.
It may expose sensitive hashes or cracked passwords if users store results carelessly.
It is not a substitute for a full identity, access, or incident response assessment.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Password Audit
use_cases.description: Assess password strength from approved hash sets and convert results into policy recommendations.

use_cases.title: Forensic Hash Recovery
use_cases.description: Plan controlled recovery steps for evidence hashes while preserving custody and data handling records.

use_cases.title: Security Training Lab
use_cases.description: Teach how attack modes affect weak passwords in a lab with synthetic hashes and safe test data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Hash Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized Hashcat audit for a small set of test hashes. Include scope checks, hash identification, attack selection, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Attack Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these authorized hash types and password policy details, recommend suitable Hashcat modes and attack strategies without exposing cracked passwords.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Controlled Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a controlled workflow for an approved password audit. Include session management, hardware constraints, result storage, and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Audit Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a password audit report for leadership and engineers. Include risk themes, policy gaps, remediation priorities, and secure disposal requirements.

output_examples.input: I have written approval to assess NTLM hashes from a test domain.
output: Confirm the exact system scope, data owner, retention period, and reporting audience.
Start with hash type validation, then use conservative dictionary and rule-based attacks before broader masks.
Report password patterns and control gaps without listing plaintext passwords in general channels.

output_examples.input: Summarize policy issues from a cracked password set.
output: Group findings by short length, dictionary words, reused patterns, seasonal terms, and missing complexity.
Recommend minimum length, blocklists, multi-factor authentication, and privileged account rotation where appropriate.
Separate executive risk themes from technical evidence kept in restricted storage.

output_examples.input: A lab cracking job is slow and the GPU is underused.
output: Check driver support, device selection, workload profile, hash mode accuracy, and optimized kernel compatibility.
Reduce the test scope before increasing workload on shared systems.
Monitor temperature and stability during longer runs.

best_practices: Verify written authorization, scope, and data handling rules before preparing any hash files.
Use isolated storage, encryption, and restricted access for hashes, potfiles, and cracked password evidence.
Report patterns and remediation priorities while minimizing plaintext password exposure.
anti_patterns: Do not crack hashes from systems, networks, or users outside the approved scope.
Do not store cracked passwords in shared tickets, chat logs, or broad-access repositories.
Do not run high-intensity cracking jobs on shared systems without resource and thermal controls.

faq.question: Does this skill run Hashcat automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command patterns that require user control and authorization.

faq.question: Can I use it for production password audits?
faq.answer: Yes, only with written authorization, defined scope, secure storage, and a clear retention plan.

faq.question: Does it identify hash types?
faq.answer: It lists common Hashcat modes and suggests validation steps before selecting an attack strategy.

faq.question: Does it include defensive guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains reporting, password policy improvements, stronger hashing, and multi-factor authentication.

faq.question: What data is most sensitive during use?
faq.answer: Hash files, potfiles, cracked passwords, source evidence, and audit reports require restricted handling.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Hashcat is required. GPU drivers, OpenCL or CUDA support, and approved wordlists may also be needed.
